item.title: How to Assume an AWS Role from Another AWS Role: A Comprehensive Guide
item.description:
How to Assume an AWS Role from Another AWS Role: A Comprehensive Guide

Managing permissions and access across different AWS accounts can be daunting, especially when you need to assume roles from one AWS account to another. This process, often referred to as “role chaining,” involves configuring your roles and permissions in AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) for secure and effective cross-account access.

Scenario Overview

Imagine you have two AWS accounts, which we’ll refer to as Account A and Account B. In Account B, a specific role (let’s call it Role-B) is set up to allow access to Assume a role in Account A (referred to as Role-A). The key policies for each role must be structured correctly, as proper configuration is essential for successful role assumption.
